exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
outcome: time to initiation of enteral feeds
time to completion of enteral feeds
cohort: 80 neonates requiring abdominal surgery within 28 days of life were enrolled, with 40 born via vaginal delivery and 40 via cesarean section.
finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with modest advantages in postoperative recovery for neonates undergoing abdominal surgery, specifically in terms of faster gastrointestinal recovery and reduced ventilatory support.
mod_finding: Neonates born via vaginal delivery showed significantly earlier initiation of enteral feeds, faster achievement of full feeds, and shorter ventilation duration compared to those born via cesarean section, after undergoing abdominal surgery.
